previous_audits.chain_closure_explanation:
The second audit has the scientifically correct tuple. The source note is not a positive theorem row; it is a scoped no-go against the direct A4 shortcut from primitive parity gate plus rank(P_A)=4 to native CAR/coframe response and action-unit pinning. The runner evidence is class A finite algebra: dimensions of generated algebras and commutants, Clifford anticommutator checks, compatible non-CAR responses, gate-sector ambiguity, exact finite half-zone checks, and the unchanged kappa rescaling degeneracy. No-Go Discipline is closed for this narrow packet scope. N1: at least five attack routes against the shortcut are tested or explicitly bounded: gate algebra dimension 2 vs Cl_4 dimension 16; commutant dimension 8 underdetermination; a single Z_2 involution not being a four-axis coframe; same gate data allowing non-CAR two-qubit responses; gate not defining odd edge maps; action-unit rescaling persistence. N2: the packet collapses the residuals to two independent walls, CAR/coframe orientation-statistics lift and dimensional action/metrology unit, without inflating subchecks as independent walls. N3: hidden imports are explicit: CAR/coframe response, primitive two-mode CAR carrier, Target 3 bridge, and metrology/action unit are marked as conditional imports or surviving routes, not smuggled into the no-go. N4: residual matching is exact because the no-go attacks only the direct A4 shortcut, while preserving the conditional parity-gate theorem once CAR/coframe response is separately supplied. N5: rhetoric is narrow to P_A H_cell finite active-block parity-gate-to-CAR non-forcing, not a universal claim that no CAR route exists. N6: partial closure paths remain open in the note: direct A1 module-morphism, orientation/statistics lift, metrology theorem, or minimal carrier/metrology axiom. N7: the strongest steelman is that the residual Z_2 half-zone inside the rank-four block may already encode the missing orientation/statistics lift; the packet answers that this assumes the CAR/coframe carrier and is defeated by underdetermination and non-CAR compatible models for the gate-alone route. N8: cross-cycle echo risk is handled within the supplied packet by carrying forward A2 rescaling degeneracy and listing A1/A4/metrology survivor paths rather than claiming broader C1 closure or retiring unrelated walls. Therefore audited_clean no_go/A is defensible at the narrow A4 shortcut scope.

The broader chain does not derive those carrier premises, the odd Clifford/CAR coframe lift, or the dimensional action unit from the supplied authorities.
previous_audits.claim_scope: Given a supplied rank-four active block and rank-two parity projector, the even Z2 gate does not force a metric-compatible Clifford/CAR coframe response or dimensional action unit; the quarter coefficient remains conditional on an imported CAR carrier.
previous_audits.load_bearing_step: The algebra generated by the parity-gate data is only span{I_K,Q_+}, with dimension 2 and an 8-dimensional commutant, so it cannot force the full M_4(C) Clifford/CAR algebra.
previous_audits.notes_for_re_audit_if_any: missing_bridge_theorem: prove or cite retained derivations of the rank-four parity carrier, the orientation/statistics lift to odd metric-compatible Clifford/CAR generators, and the dimensional action-unit bridge, then add current-cycle N1-N8 resolution tests.
previous_audits.verdict_rationale: The class-A finite algebra correctly shows that one rank-two projector leaves a large commutant and admits non-CAR responses. N1 tests algebra, alternate-carrier, and unit-rescaling attacks, while N2-N4 expose independent CAR/coframe and action-unit imports without a retained prior residual witness. N5 lacks five-resolution execution evidence; N6 finds no supplied approved primitive closing the lift; N7 lacks an independent retained steelman resolution; and N8 echoes are unretained index records rather than closing authorities. The narrow boundary is therefore supported only on supplied carrier data, not cleanly derived from the restricted premise packet.
